page: Microsoft Azure D2ps_v7 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine within the Dpsv7 series, provisioned via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs built on 64-bit arm64 processor architecture and includes 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not incorporate hardware accelerators or graphical processing units (0 GPUs).

Storage architecture on the D2ps_v7 relies entirely on remote storage solutions, as the instance provides no local disk capacity. The configuration supports Azure Premium Storage, requiring external managed disks for the operating system and application storage layers. Operating on arm64 hardware requires workloads and runtime dependencies to support the ARM instruction set, differing from traditional x86 server profiles while offering predictable performance through dedicated CPU thread allocations rather than burstable credit models.

Resource allocation delivers a balanced compute-to-memory footprint suitable for Linux-based open-source stacks optimized for ARM. Microsoft Azure D2ps_v7 is designed for general-purpose workloads, including lightweight web serving, application microservices, API backends, small containerized environments, and continuous integration runners.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ps_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and powered by an arm64 CPU architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote Azure Premium Storage options for persistent disk volumes. Featuring dedicated core provisioning, D2ps_v7 provides steady compute performance for environments compiled for 64-bit ARM. The balanced hardware ratio and dedicated thread model make this instance suited for containerized applications, lightweight web servers, entry-level microservices, and development environments.
